record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: For a phase-type distribution whose Laplace transform is f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s), with p and q coprime, deg p=2, and deg q=3, what necessary and sufficient conditions guarantee that the distribution has a phase-type representation with exactly three transient states? The question is to go beyond the known order-three condition for the special reciprocal cubic case with one real pole and one complex-conjugate pole pair.

evidence.quote: A more interesting problem, both from the theoretical and practical points of view, would be the characterization of order 3 PH-distributions.

Problem 5: Consider a PH-distribution whose Laplace transform is f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s), where p(s) has degree two and q(s) degree three. Under which conditions (besides condition (43)) has this distribution an order 3 representation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A continuous phase-type (PH) distribution is the distribution of the time until absorption of a finite-state, continuous-time Markov chain with one absorbing state and finitely many transient states. Equivalently, it is the distribution on $[0,\infty)$ with density $f(t)=\boldsymbol{\alpha}\,e^{T t}\boldsymbol{T}^{0}$ (and possibly an atom at $0$), where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is a sub-stochastic row vector, $T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is a sub-generator (off-diagonal entries non-negative, row sums non-positive, non-singular), and $\boldsymbol{T}^{0}=-T\mathbf{1}$. The smallest such $n$ is the order of the distribution; the pair $(\boldsymbol{\alpha},T)$ is called a representation of order $n$.

The Laplace–Stieltjes transform of any PH-distribution is a rational function $\widetilde{f}(s)=p(s)/q(s)$ with $p,q$ coprime polynomials, $\deg p<\deg q$, and the pole of $\widetilde{f}$ of maximal real part is real, simple, and negative.

Problem. Let $\widetilde{f}(s)=p(s)/q(s)$ be the Laplace–Stieltjes transform of a PH-distribution, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime, $\deg p=2$, and $\deg q=3$. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $p$ and $q$ for $\widetilde{f}$ to admit a PH-representation with exactly three transient states (i.e.\ the order of the distribution equals $3$), extending the known characterization that covers only the special "reciprocal cubic" case in which $q$ has one real root and a pair of complex-conjugate roots.
artifact.status_search_result: A full characterization of order-3 PH-distributions in terms of their rational Laplace transform appears not to be known. Existing literature provides canonical representations of PH(3) and partial results (e.g. Horváth–Telek's canonical form, pole-based lower bounds, and characterizations for the reciprocal-cubic case with one real pole and a complex-conjugate pair), but no general necessary-and-sufficient condition for arbitrary $p/q$ with $\deg p=2$, $\deg q=3$ to admit a 3-state PH representation has been identified.

status_evidence.title: A Canonical Representation of Order 3 Phase Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Canonical representation of PH(3) distributions and characterization via moments / Laplace transform coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Order-3 PH-distributions admit canonical representations, but a general necessary-and-sufficient condition on p/q for order 3 is not established.

status_evidence.title: The Order of Phase-Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on the number of states needed to represent a PH-distribution are derived based on poles of its Laplace-Stieltjes transform.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (lower-bound) results are known for the minimal order question.
